findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple items (sandwiches and cut vegetables) in the double door standing cooler nearest the cafeteria to be without date marking. When the inspector asked the date the items were prepped it was stated that the items were prepared on Tuesday (09/02). CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) placed dates on the items. Food being cold held for more than 24 hours must be used or discarded within seven days. Date marking helps to prevent foods from being held past an unsafe date. Educate all employees about date marking requirements.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the two dish plates in the facility to not be operational. The PIC has communicated with maintenance to obtain new batteries for the temperature measuring devices. Inspector will return on 09/15/25 to check that the batteries in both heat plates have been replaced, and both devices are working. When a facility is using heat for sanitation purposes there must be heat detection plates. Facility should use plates on a regular basis to ensure the proper sanitizing temperature is being reached (160F+).
findings.citation_text: 4-302.13(A) Temperature Measuring Devices, Manual and Mechanical Warewashing. (A) In manual WAREWASHING operations, a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be provided and readily accessible for frequently measuring the washing and SANITIZING temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
No ambient thermometers were observed inside the coolers throughout the kitchen. Ensure ambient thermometers are placed in any cold cooler that holds TCS foods.
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Sanitizer bucket observed with a quat concentration of 100ppm. CORRECTED- Upon request, employee remade sanitizer bucket. Sanitizer observed at 400ppm quat.
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have concentration based on label (200-400ppm). [P]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Final rinse temperature dial on the dish machine is not functional. Dial remains pointing at 80-90F regardless of actual rinse temperature as measured by a plate type dishwasher thermometer. 
4-204.115: A WAREWASHING machine shall be equipped with a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE that indicates the temperature of the water: (A) In each wash and rinse tank; (B) As the water enters the hot water SANITIZING final rinse manifold or in the chemical SANITIZING solution tank. [Pf]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Employee doing salad bar prep was observed using the handwashing sink at the end of the service line to wash produce. Proper use of handwashing sinks and washing produce at the prep sink were discussed. Produce was taken to prep sink to be washed prior to prep.
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Cease the practice of using handwashing sinks for other purposes.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Sani-buckets were observed with concentration below 100ppm quat while the 3 part sink was observed at proper concentration of 200ppm quat. Sani-buckets were prepared for use upon arrival of staff and were used to wipe down tables prior to arrival of inspector. Concentration was worn down from use. Fresh sanitizer solutions were provided at 200ppm. Ensure solutions are changed frequently/between uses as needed throughout the day and maintained at proper concentration.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-703.11 Employee was observed at the 3 part sink quickly dunking a knife in sanitizer solution prior to setting it aside to air dry during ware washing. Proper contact time of at least 30 seconds was discussed. Knife was placed back in the sanitizer solution to allow for proper contact time during sanitization. 
After being cleaned, equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in chemical manual operations, including the application of sanitizing chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods, using a solution as specified under § 4-501.114 (in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions). Contact time shall be consistent with those on EPA-registered label use instructions by providing at least 30 seconds for quaternary ammonia chemical sanitizing solutions.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Portions of cheese shreds were observed in a large pan at the service line where salad bar prep was underway. Cheese shreds were observed at 54F-57F. Cheese shreds were portioned the Friday prior and were pulled from the cooler this morning to be further portioned into a smaller container for use during lunch. Prep was occurring in the 9 o’clock hour, and salad bar would not be set up until closer to 10:40am. Cheese shreds were placed in a freezer to quickly drop the temperature prior to storing in the cooler until closer to time for service. PIC was advised to have staff get out only what they need as they are working on prep to limit time TCS foods spend in the temperature danger zone.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Sani-buckets were observed with concentration of 0ppm quat while the 3 part sink was observed at proper concentration of 200ppm quat. Sanitizer container connected to the dispenser was less than a quarter full and air bubbles were observed in the suction line. A new sanitizer container was connected to the dispenser, and freshly dispensed solutions in the sani-buckets were observed at 200ppm. Kitchen staff were advised to allow the dispenser to run for several seconds prior to filling buckets and the 3 part sink to allow proper suction and removal of air bubbles that may interfere with product flow and to verify proper concentration with quat test strips.    
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.
